title: Aviation Weekly Market Report
headline: Supply-side risk eased for both OEMs: labour deals ratified at Airbus Spain and Boeing, and the FAA closed the 737 MAX software scare - while Middle East airspace risk widened.
summary: Airbus workers in Spain ended months of strikes (76.76% backed the deal) and SPEEA members ratified four-year contracts with Boeing on October 1.
An FAA review board found the 737 MAX U14 software issue not safety-critical on October 2, putting MAX 10 certification back on track for customers such as Ryanair and Alaska.
Houthis told airlines to avoid Saudi airspace on October 5, after EASA had already advised avoiding part of the Jeddah FIR on September 30.
Air cargo enters peak season on fuel-driven rates: Hong Kong-North America averaged $7.02/kg in September, 31% up year on year, with IATA putting August jet fuel 79.2% above a year earlier.
AerCap signed 85 leases and bought 20 737 MAX in Q3, while KLM took its first A350-900 and British Airways turned 75% of its A380 seats premium.

sections.title: Safety & regulation
sections.takeaway: One certification risk closed; one airspace risk opened.

items.headline: FAA board clears 737 MAX flight-computer software issue
items.so_what: With the U14 glitch judged not safety-critical, the MAX 10 can join the MAX 7 in clearing its last regulatory hurdle - capacity Ryanair and Alaska Airlines have on order.
items.detail: The FAA's Corrective Action Review Board concluded on October 2 that pilots retain full control and the indications are clear.

sources.title: Boeing's Path to Max 10 Certification Looks Clear Again

items.headline: Houthis warn airlines off Saudi airspace
items.so_what: Adds Saudi skies to the Middle East routes carriers must plan around, on top of EASA's September 30 advice to avoid part of the Jeddah FIR at all altitudes.
items.detail: The warning named no airports, routes or timetable. EASA still recommends against flights over Iran and Jordan at any altitude.

sources.title: Houthis warn airlines to avoid Saudi airspace as Yemen conflict escalates

sections.title: Airlines
sections.takeaway: Premium long-haul growth at the network carriers, retrenchment in the Baltics, and cargo yields rising into the peak.

items.headline: British Airways turns 75% of its A380 seats premium
items.so_what: All 12 BA A380s are being refitted with more than 35,000 parts each as part of a £7 billion transformation plan.

sources.title: Fewer seats, more luxury: step into the new British Airways A380 interiors

items.headline: KLM takes its first A350-900
items.so_what: 331 seats in three classes, including 34 business suites, for long-haul routes from Schiphol such as Toronto - as KLM continues renewing its long-haul fleet.

sources.title: KLM takes delivery of first A350-900

items.headline: Delta-LATAM joint venture up 31% in capacity in four years
items.so_what: Combined capacity rose about 31% in 2026 compared with 2023, across 28 joint routes and 17.4 million customers since October 2022.

sources.title: Delta and LATAM mark four years of Joint Venture with 31% increase in capacity and 17.4 million customers carried between North and South America

items.headline: airBaltic to cut 500-700 roles and shrink its A220-300 fleet
items.so_what: 500-700 of about 3,000 staff go as the carrier leans on year-round ACMI partners instead of its own aircraft.

sources.title: airBaltic plans up to 700 job cuts as it reshapes business

items.headline: Air cargo heads into peak on fuel-driven rates
items.so_what: Hong Kong-North America averaged $7.02/kg in September (31% up year on year); Cirium finds no major hub has run dry since the Strait of Hormuz closed, but smaller airports have.
items.detail: IATA put August jet fuel 79.2% above a year earlier and demand up 4.4%. CH Robinson warns that if freighter capacity follows technology demand to the US, Europe-bound shippers will have fewer options.

sources.title: Airfreight rates edge up in September
Major hubs unaffected by jet fuel supply issues
Peak season pressure to develop unevenly across origins and cargo types

sections.title: Manufacturers & supply chain
sections.takeaway: Labour peace at both OEMs and new final assembly capacity in Germany, against a narrowbody backlog the duopoly still owns.

items.headline: Airbus Spain and Boeing's SPEEA engineers ratify new contracts
items.so_what: Removes the risk of strikes deepening production problems at both manufacturers: 76.76% of voting Airbus staff in Spain backed the deal, and SPEEA ratified Boeing's four-year offers.
items.detail: Airbus Spain staff had begun an indefinite strike on August 25; Airbus has more than 14,000 staff in Spain.

sources.title: Relief for both Airbus and Boeing as thousands of workers back new contracts

items.headline: Deutsche Aircraft opens D328eco final assembly in Leipzig
items.so_what: The more than €100 million site is designed for up to 48 aircraft a year and moves the D328eco into serial production.

sources.title: Deutsche Aircraft opens Leipzig plant for D328eco production

items.headline: Narrowbody backlog of 13,500: Airbus 56%, Boeing 36%
items.so_what: Airbus holds 56% of the global backlog of latest-generation narrowbodies and Boeing 36%, the context for Leeham's look at Comac's 1,100-aircraft backlog.
items.detail: Leeham counts orders for over 20,500 of the newest-generation narrowbodies, about 7,000 delivered. The analysis itself is behind a subscription; only the free opening was read.

sources.title: About That 1,100-Aircraft Comac Backlog

sections.title: Finance & leasing
sections.takeaway: The largest lessor kept recycling its portfolio into new-technology narrowbodies, and a Turkish low-cost carrier closed a European acquisition.

items.headline: AerCap signs 85 leases and buys 20 737 MAX in Q3
items.so_what: Purchases of 32 aircraft included eight A320neo-family jets and 20 737 MAX, while 65 aircraft were sold - and about $783 million went on share buybacks.
items.detail: Leases covered 16 wide-bodies, 45 narrow-bodies, 13 engines and 11 helicopters; financing transactions came to about $900 million.

sources.title: AerCap reports strong Q3 transactions

items.headline: Pegasus completes its takeover of Smartwings
items.so_what: The Turkish carrier now controls the Czech Republic's largest airline group, including the CSA Czech Airlines brand, after giving up some Prague-Antalya slots to win approval.
items.detail: Pegasus had offered €154 million for 100% of the group in December 2025.

sources.title: Pegasus Airlines completes its acquisition of Czech group Smartwings

sections.title: Defence & space
sections.takeaway: Missile-defence and fighter demand is reaching production lines, and India's transport competition is shaping industrial bids.

items.headline: Boeing wins $14.7 billion to triple PAC-3 MSE seeker output
items.so_what: A seven-year plan to triple seeker production for Lockheed Martin's Patriot interceptor, after seeker deliveries already rose more than 30% in 2025.

sources.title: Boeing wins $14.7 billion contract to triple Patriot missile seeker production

items.headline: F-16 deliveries move: Taiwan's first Block 70s, Morocco's first Block 72 flies
items.so_what: Taiwan received the first two of 66 Block 70s - deliveries were due to begin in 2023 and were held up by the F-16 line's relocation, supply-chain and software problems; Morocco's first Block 72 is in flight test.
items.detail: More Taiwanese jets are due before the end of 2026 and the rest in 2027-2028; the two delivered arrived without their Viper Shield electronic-warfare systems.

sources.title: Taiwan receives first two of 66 F-16V Block 70 jets amid rising Chinese pressure
Lockheed Martin Announces First Flight of Morocco's First F 16 Block 72

items.headline: Embraer and Mahindra pick Nagpur for a C-390 line
items.so_what: Positions the C-390 against Lockheed Martin and Tata's C-130J-30 for India's 60-aircraft Medium Transport Aircraft programme, with a site ready to build on if India selects it.

sources.title: Embraer, Mahindra pick Nagpur for potential C-390 assembly line

items.headline: Airbus completes the first 32 OneWeb replacement satellites
items.so_what: The first tranche of 669 spacecraft Eutelsat has on order, heading to SpaceX for launch, towards 1,300 OneWeb satellites in orbit by 2030.

sources.title: Airbus Completes First 32 OneWeb Replenishment Satellites for Eutelsat Fleet Refresh

sections.title: Sustainability
sections.takeaway: Airlines want CORSIA, not the EU ETS, to be the global carbon framework.

items.headline: IATA marks ten years of CORSIA as the EU reviews its ETS
items.so_what: More than 130 countries take part and CORSIA should have mitigated about 200 million tonnes of CO2 by year-end; IATA wants the EU's ETS review - which considers covering destinations within 5,000 km - to reinforce CORSIA, not overlap it.

sources.title: Ten Years on from CORSIA Agreement, Governments Must Strengthen the Global Framework for Aviation Emissions
